summary: Full read-only security audit of the WisdomBI prod database: RLS, SECURITY DEFINER, grants/views/extensions, service-role boundary
logs: 5 finders sweeping prod catalog + code, read-only

confirmed.title: Unauthenticated SECURITY DEFINER RPC overwrites/deletes ANY tenant's forecast (no auth check)
confirmed.evidence: pg_get_functiondef shows prosecdef=true, SET search_path='public', and the body performs UPDATE public.financial_forecasts SET assumptions/assumptions_published_at WHERE id=p_forecast_id; DELETE FROM public.forecast_pl_lines WHERE forecast_id=p_forecast_id AND is_manual=false (when p_force_full_replace); and an INSERT ... ON CONFLICT upsert of caller-supplied P&L lines — with NO reference to auth.uid()/auth_can_manage_business/system_roles anywhere. aclexplode(proacl) => grantee IN {anon,authenticated} (risky_grantees='anon,authenticated'). Definer execution bypasses the (correct) forecast_pl_lines/financial_forecasts RLS policies. PostgREST exposes it at POST /rest/v1/rpc/save_assumptions_and_materialize callable with the public anon key. A caller who supplies another tenant's forecast_id can wipe (force_full_replace) and rewrite that tenant's entire forecast P&L and republish attacker-controlled assumptions. Gating condition: knowledge of a target forecast_id UUID (financial_forecasts SELECT is RLS-gated, so cross-tenant IDs are not enumerable via the table, but they appear in that tenant's own URLs/API responses).
confirmed.remediation: REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.save_assumptions_and_materialize(uuid,jsonb,jsonb,boolean) FROM anon, authenticated; grant only to service_role (the API route already runs server-side and should assert auth_can_manage_business on the forecast's business_id). Re-issue the REVOKE after every DROP+CREATE. Optionally add an internal guard: SELECT business_id INTO v_biz FROM financial_forecasts WHERE id=p_forecast_id; IF NOT auth_can_manage_business(v_biz) THEN RAISE EXCEPTION.

verdict.reasoning: Live catalog confirms save_assumptions_and_materialize(uuid,jsonb,jsonb,boolean) oid 147803 is SECURITY DEFINER (owner postgres, search_path=public) with proacl granting EXECUTE to BOTH anon and authenticated ({postgres=X,anon=X,authenticated=X,service_role=X}). pg_get_functiondef shows the sole guard is an existence check (IF NOT EXISTS SELECT 1 FROM financial_forecasts WHERE id=p_forecast_id THEN RAISE) — no auth.uid()/auth_can_manage_business/role check anywhere. As DEFINER it bypasses RLS and performs UPDATE financial_forecasts SET assumptions/assumptions_published_at, DELETE forecast_pl_lines WHERE is_manual=false (on p_force_full_replace), and upsert of caller-supplied P&L lines. It is reachable unauthenticated via PostgREST POST /rest/v1/rpc/save_assumptions_and_materialize with the public anon key. This is a genuine definer write primitive with a weak guard exposed to anon — the write primitive is real. HOWEVER the destructive exploit against a specific victim requires knowing that tenant's forecast_id UUID, and that condition is genuinely limiting: financial_forecasts RLS is ENABLED (relrowsecurity=true) with a correctly business-scoped policy (USING auth_is_super_admin() OR business_id = ANY(auth_get_accessible_business_ids())), and forecast_pl_lines RLS is enabled and scoped through the parent forecast — so neither anon nor any authenticated user can enumerate another tenant's forecast_id. A 122-bit UUID is not guessable. The legitimate route (src/app/api/forecast/[id]/recompute/route.ts:44) uses an auth-bound client with its own getUser()+business check, so the anon/authenticated grant is unnecessary surface, not a requirement. Rubric fit: HIGH matches on both stated prongs — 'a definer write primitive with weak guard' AND 'needs a condition (a known id)'. Not CRITICAL because there is no reachable cross-tenant enumeration path to obtain a victim forecast_id, so no unauthenticated or arbitrary-authenticated principal can write a specific other client's data without an out-of-band id. Finding CONFIRMED at HIGH; the finder's HIGH [unauthenticated] rating and remediation (REVOKE FROM anon, authenticated; grant service_role only; add internal auth_can_manage_business guard) are correct. Proof queries: pg_proc (prosecdef/proacl), pg_get_functiondef(147803), pg_policy on financial_forecasts/forecast_pl_lines, pg_class.relrowsecurity both true.

confirmed.title: Unauthenticated SECURITY DEFINER RPC deactivates/injects active forecasts for ANY business (no auth check)
confirmed.evidence: pg_get_functiondef: prosecdef=true, no auth.uid()/guard. Body: UPDATE public.financial_forecasts SET is_active=false WHERE business_id=p_business_id AND fiscal_year=... AND is_active=true; then INSERT a new is_active=true forecast for p_business_id with caller-supplied JSONB. proacl grants anon,authenticated (risky_grantees='anon,authenticated'). Bypasses financial_forecasts RLS. Reachable at POST /rest/v1/rpc/create_active_forecast_locked with the anon key. A caller supplying another tenant's business_id can flip that tenant's current active forecast to inactive (corrupting all downstream reporting) and inject a bogus active forecast. business_id (businesses.id) is comparatively discoverable — only ~18 businesses, and ids appear in client URLs/API payloads.
confirmed.remediation: REVOKE EXECUTE ... FROM anon, authenticated (leave service_role). The calling API route must assert auth_can_manage_business(p_business_id) before invoking, or add that check inside the function. Re-issue REVOKE after any DROP+CREATE.

verdict.reasoning: Live catalog confirms the exploit primitive exactly. public.create_active_forecast_locked(uuid,integer,text,jsonb): prosecdef=true, owner=postgres, proacl={postgres=X,anon=X,authenticated=X,service_role=X} — anon AND authenticated hold EXECUTE. pg_get_functiondef shows NO internal authorization check (no auth.uid(), no auth_can_access_business, no is_super_admin); it unconditionally UPDATE financial_forecasts SET is_active=false WHERE business_id=p_business_id AND fiscal_year=... AND is_active=true, then INSERTs a new is_active=true row for the caller-supplied p_business_id from caller JSONB. As SECURITY DEFINER owned by postgres it bypasses financial_forecasts RLS. It is exposed over PostgREST at POST /rest/v1/rpc/create_active_forecast_locked and callable with the PUBLIC anon key, bypassing the ownership/withSchema checks in src/app/api/forecast-wizard-v4/generate/route.ts (line 307). The sibling activate_forecast_locked grants only {authenticated,service_role} (no anon), confirming this anon grant is anomalous and not required. Reachable path: an attacker POSTs to the rpc with the anon key, p_business_id = a target tenant's forecast business id, p_fiscal_year, and a JSONB body → flips that tenant's active forecast to inactive (corrupting downstream reporting) and injects a bogus active forecast. NEUTRALIZING NUANCE fixing severity at HIGH (not CRITICAL): the write requires a KNOWN valid business id. The route actually passes profileId (business_profiles.id space, not businesses.id as the finder wrote — minor evidence inaccuracy, no effect on exploitability), and that UUID is not enumerable by a truly unauthenticated caller; only a caller who already knows a target id (or any authenticated user who can obtain one) can drive it. That 'needs a known id' condition is exactly the rubric's HIGH clause / 'definer write primitive with weak guard.' The search_path IS set (no hijack vector), but that does not remove the missing-auth hole. Remediation stands: REVOKE EXECUTE FROM anon, authenticated (match the sibling), re-issue after any DROP+CREATE.

confirmed.title: save_assumptions_and_materialize: anon-granted, no internal auth — overwrites/DELETEs any tenant's forecast P&L by forecast_id
confirmed.evidence: proacl = 'postgres=X/postgres | anon=X/postgres | authenticated=X/postgres | service_role=X/postgres' (anon can EXECUTE). Body's ONLY check is `IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM financial_forecasts WHERE id = p_forecast_id)` — no ownership/coach/uid check. It then `UPDATE financial_forecasts SET assumptions=…` and, when p_force_full_replace=true, `DELETE FROM forecast_pl_lines WHERE forecast_id=p_forecast_id AND is_manual=false`, then bulk-upserts P&L lines. The app's guard is route-only: src/app/api/forecast-wizard-v4/generate/route.ts:29 uses createRouteHandlerClient() and checks businessId ownership at :58-91 — but the RPC is exposed at POST /rest/v1/rpc/save_assumptions_and_materialize to the public anon key, bypassing that route. A caller who knows a forecast_id UUID can wipe and rewrite another client's forecast.
confirmed.remediation: REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.save_assumptions_and_materialize(uuid,jsonb,jsonb,boolean) FROM anon, authenticated; and call it only from the service-role client (like the 5 account fns fixed today), OR add an internal guard: `IF NOT public.auth_can_manage_business((SELECT business_id FROM financial_forecasts WHERE id=p_forecast_id)) THEN RAISE EXCEPTION` and keep the grant. Re-issue the REVOKE after any DROP+CREATE.

verdict.reasoning: Live catalog confirms the finding on every load-bearing fact. proacl = {postgres=X/postgres,anon=X/postgres,authenticated=X/postgres,service_role=X/postgres} — anon AND authenticated both hold EXECUTE (today's revoke sweep did not cover this function). pg_get_functiondef confirms SECURITY DEFINER, owner postgres, SET search_path=public; the ONLY internal check is IF NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM financial_forecasts WHERE id=p_forecast_id) — no ownership/coach/uid/auth_can_manage_business guard. It then UPDATEs financial_forecasts (overwriting assumptions + stamping assumptions_published_at), and when p_force_full_replace=true DELETEs forecast_pl_lines WHERE forecast_id=p_forecast_id AND is_manual=false, then bulk-upserts P&L lines. As a definer function it bypasses RLS on both tables. Being a public-schema function with anon EXECUTE, it is exposed at POST /rest/v1/rpc/save_assumptions_and_materialize to the public anon key; the route-level ownership guard in generate/route.ts does not protect the RPC. Concrete reachable path: any caller (unauthenticated anon key, which ships in the browser bundle) who possesses a target forecast_id UUID can wipe and rewrite another client's forecast P&L. This is NOT CRITICAL because a condition is required: knowledge of a foreign forecast_id UUID. anon cannot enumerate one — financial_forecasts has RLS enabled and its sole policy rls_access is scoped to role authenticated only (USING business_id = ANY(auth_get_accessible_business_ids())); there is NO anon policy, so anon direct SELECT is default-deny and returns zero rows, and v4 UUIDs are unguessable. That "needs a known id" condition places it exactly at the HIGH tier of the rubric (and it is independently a definer write primitive with an absent guard = HIGH). Severity HIGH is correct as filed; verdict CONFIRMED.

confirmed.title: create_active_forecast_locked: anon-granted, no internal auth — deactivates + inserts financial_forecasts for any business_id
confirmed.evidence: proacl grants anon+authenticated EXECUTE. Body has zero authorization logic: it takes p_business_id (businesses.id space — confirmed by route comment src/app/api/forecast-wizard-v4/generate/route.ts:58 'businessId is businesses.id'), runs `UPDATE financial_forecasts SET is_active=false WHERE business_id=p_business_id AND fiscal_year=… AND is_active=true`, then INSERTs a new active forecast (user_id taken from caller-supplied p_row). Reachable directly via /rest/v1/rpc with the anon key; the ownership check at route :58-91 is bypassed. A caller knowing a business_id UUID can deactivate a client's live forecast and inject a forged active one.
confirmed.remediation: REVOKE EXECUTE … FROM anon, authenticated and invoke via service-role only, OR add `IF NOT public.auth_can_manage_business(p_business_id) THEN RAISE EXCEPTION USING ERRCODE='42501'` at the top. Its sibling activate_forecast_locked already has no anon grant — match that.

verdict.reasoning:
Reachable exploit path confirmed, and HIGH (not CRITICAL) is the correct rating because it is gated by a known-id condition.

CATALOG PROOF: public.create_active_forecast_locked(uuid,integer,text,jsonb) is prosecdef=true with proacl {postgres=X,anon=X,authenticated=X,service_role=X}. pg_get_functiondef shows the entire body is: pg_advisory_xact_lock -> UPDATE financial_forecasts SET is_active=false WHERE business_id=p_business_id AND fiscal_year=p_fiscal_year AND forecast_type=p_forecast_type AND is_active=true -> INSERT a new is_active=true row (user_id and all financial fields taken from caller-supplied p_row jsonb) -> RETURN new id. There is NO internal authorization check (no auth.uid(), no auth_can_* guard, no is_super_admin). financial_forecasts has RLS enabled (relrowsecurity=true) but SECURITY DEFINER runs as owner postgres and bypasses RLS.

REACHABILITY: Function is in the PostgREST-exposed public schema with EXECUTE granted to anon, so an unauthenticated caller holding the public publishable anon key can POST /rest/v1/rpc/create_active_forecast_locked and the body runs as definer, entirely bypassing the app-level ownership/team/coach check in src/app/api/forecast-wizard-v4/generate/route.ts:58-97. That route uses the RLS-respecting createRouteHandlerClient and requires supabase.auth.getUser() (route.ts:31-34), so the anon grant is not needed by the legitimate flow — it is a superfluous, anomalous grant. The sibling activate_forecast_locked has {authenticated,service_role} only (no anon), confirming anon is the outlier here. authenticated=X IS required by design (the route calls the RPC as the authenticated role), but any-logged-in-user can equally call it directly against ANOTHER tenant's id, bypassing the route guard — a cross-tenant write primitive.

CONDITION THAT CAPS SEVERITY AT HIGH: The damage requires a valid victim business_profiles.id. The route actually passes p_business_id=profileId (business_profiles-space; the finding's businesses.id claim is inaccurate but immaterial), and financial_forecasts.business_id has a FK to business_profiles(id). The whole function is one implicit transaction: if p_business_id / p_row->>'user_id' do not reference real rows, the INSERT trips the FK/cast and rolls back the preceding is_active=false UPDATE too — so a random or wrong id yields no persisted damage. business_profiles.id defaults to uuid_generate_v4() (random v4), and profile UUIDs are not exposed to anon anywhere, so the target id is a genuine precondition, not free. Per the rubric, an any-principal write that needs a known id is HIGH, not CRITICAL. With a known victim business_profiles.id, the exploit fully succeeds: it deactivates the client's live forecast and commits a forged is_active=true forecast with attacker-chosen financials and user_id.

VERDICT: CONFIRMED at HIGH (matches the finder's rating; not inflated to CRITICAL because the random FK-enforced UUID is a real barrier, and not refuted because no DB-level guard neutralizes the anon/authenticated direct-RPC path). Remediation as stated is correct: REVOKE EXECUTE FROM anon (and consider authenticated, adding an internal auth_can_manage_business guard since the route already authorizes) to match sibling activate_forecast_locked. Note save_assumptions_and_materialize carries the identical anon grant and warrants the same treatment.

confirmed.title: SECURITY DEFINER write RPC create_active_forecast_locked is EXECUTE-granted to anon with no internal authorization check — unauthenticated cross-tenant forecast hijack
confirmed.evidence: Catalog: SELECT proname, prosecdef, execute_grantees FROM pg_proc → create_active_forecast_locked: security_definer=true, execute_grantees='postgres,anon,authenticated,service_role'. Function body (pg_get_functiondef) contains ZERO auth/ownership check — it takes p_business_id as a parameter, PERFORM pg_advisory_xact_lock(...), then UPDATE financial_forecasts SET is_active=false WHERE business_id=p_business_id ... and INSERT a new is_active=true row from attacker-supplied p_row jsonb. Because it is SECURITY DEFINER (owner postgres) it BYPASSES RLS. The only authorization is in the route handler src/app/api/forecast-wizard-v4/generate/route.ts:29-59 (createRouteHandlerClient + auth.getUser() + resolveBusinessProfileIds) — a direct PostgREST call POST /rest/v1/rpc/create_active_forecast_locked with the PUBLIC anon apikey bypasses that layer entirely. Reachable because 'public' is a PostgREST-exposed schema and anon holds EXECUTE (same reachability that made the 5 account RPCs exploitable before today's fix).
confirmed.remediation: REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.create_active_forecast_locked(uuid,integer,text,jsonb) FROM anon, authenticated; leave only service_role/postgres (the legit caller runs server-side). If the authenticated path must keep DB-level EXECUTE, add an internal guard: verify auth.uid() owns/can-access p_business_id via auth_can_access_business(p_business_id) and RAISE on failure. Sibling activate_forecast_locked already omits anon — match it.

verdict.reasoning: CONFIRMED core defect: public.create_active_forecast_locked(uuid,integer,text,jsonb) is SECURITY DEFINER (owner postgres, bypasses RLS), proacl={postgres,anon,authenticated,service_role} (anon+authenticated hold EXECUTE), and pg_get_functiondef shows ZERO internal auth/ownership check — it deactivates the caller-named business's active forecast and inserts an attacker-shaped is_active=true row. Sibling activate_forecast_locked correctly omits anon. So it is a genuine definer write primitive with no guard, exposed to anon+authenticated. However the finder's CRITICAL 'unauthenticated cross-tenant hijack' overstates reachability: (1) financial_forecasts.business_id has FK -> business_profiles(id); a guessed/random UUID fails the FK, and since the whole function is one implicit transaction the destructive UPDATE rolls back with the failed INSERT (xact-scoped advisory lock released), so damage requires a VALID existing business_profiles.id. (2) businesses, business_profiles and financial_forecasts all have RLS enabled with policies bound to role 'authenticated' ONLY — no anon policies exist, so anon direct-table reads default-DENY and anon cannot harvest a valid id from these tables. Thus a pure-unauthenticated targeted exploit is not self-contained; it needs an out-of-band known valid business_profiles.id. This is precisely the rubric's HIGH pattern: 'a definer write primitive with weak guard' AND 'needs a condition (a known id)'. Realistic path: any authenticated principal (one of ~18 clients/coaches) supplies another tenant's business_profiles.id (which appears in app URLs/payloads) to deactivate that tenant's active forecast and plant an attacker-controlled active forecast, bypassing RLS — cross-tenant write, gated on a known id. Remediation valid: REVOKE EXECUTE from anon,authenticated to match activate_forecast_locked and add an internal auth_can_access_business(p_business_id) guard. Evidence: pg_proc.proacl/prosecdef/proconfig and pg_get_functiondef for create_active_forecast_locked; FK financial_forecasts_business_id_fkey REFERENCES business_profiles(id); pg_policy rows show only authenticated-role policies on all three tables; bypassed route src/app/api/forecast-wizard-v4/generate/route.ts.

confirmed.title: SECURITY DEFINER write/delete RPC save_assumptions_and_materialize is EXECUTE-granted to anon with no authorization check — unauthenticated can wipe and rewrite any forecast's P&L lines
confirmed.evidence: Catalog: pg_proc shows security_definer=true, execute_grantees='postgres,anon,authenticated,service_role'. Body (pg_get_functiondef) only checks EXISTS(forecast id) — no auth.uid()/ownership check. It UPDATEs financial_forecasts.assumptions + assumptions_published_at (publishes) for arbitrary p_forecast_id, and when p_force_full_replace=true executes DELETE FROM forecast_pl_lines WHERE forecast_id=p_forecast_id AND is_manual=false before inserting attacker-supplied p_pl_lines. SECURITY DEFINER bypasses RLS. Direct PostgREST RPC with the public anon key bypasses the route-handler authorization (src/app/api/forecast-wizard-v4/generate/route.ts:370, seed-from-prior/route.ts:241, forecast/[id]/recompute/route.ts:165 all call it via the RLS-respecting authenticated client — the DB never re-checks the caller).
confirmed.remediation: REVOKE EXECUTE ... FROM anon, authenticated; keep service_role/postgres only, OR add an internal guard resolving the forecast's business and calling auth_can_access_business(...) before any write. p_force_full_replace makes the destructive DELETE reachable by an unauthenticated caller — highest priority to close.

verdict.reasoning: Catalog confirms the primitive: save_assumptions_and_materialize(uuid,jsonb,jsonb,boolean) is SECURITY DEFINER (runs as postgres, bypasses RLS) with proacl {postgres,anon,authenticated,service_role} all holding EXECUTE. The body's only guard is IF NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM financial_forecasts WHERE id=p_forecast_id) — no auth.uid()/ownership/tenant check. It UPDATEs+publishes financial_forecasts.assumptions/assumptions_published_at and, on p_force_full_replace=true, DELETEs forecast_pl_lines WHERE forecast_id=p_forecast_id AND is_manual=false before inserting caller-supplied lines. So it is a genuine definer write/delete primitive reachable via PostgREST RPC by the public anon key. However, the destructive/write path is GATED on supplying a valid p_forecast_id: the EXISTS check requires the forecast to exist, and a forecast_id is a 122-bit random UUID. Both financial_forecasts and forecast_pl_lines have RLS ENABLED with a single policy (rls_access) scoped to the {authenticated} role and constrained by auth_get_accessible_business_ids()/auth_can_manage_business(); there is NO anon policy, so anon direct SELECT is default-denied (the anon table DML grants are inert under RLS). Therefore anon cannot enumerate forecast ids through any API path, and an authenticated client's reads are RLS-scoped to their own businesses so they cannot enumerate another tenant's forecast ids either. The ungated CRITICAL claim ('unauthenticated can wipe ANY forecast') is not reachable: it requires an out-of-band-leaked foreign forecast_id UUID that neither anon nor a cross-tenant authenticated user can obtain via the exposed API. This matches the rubric's HIGH tier exactly — a definer write primitive with a weak guard that additionally needs a known id/condition. The finding is real and the remediation (REVOKE EXECUTE FROM anon, authenticated, leaving {postgres,service_role}, consistent with the five functions fixed 23 Aug) should be applied; only the severity is overstated. (Caveat: if any anon-readable view/function elsewhere leaks forecast_ids, the pure-unauthenticated path would become ungated and this returns to CRITICAL — none was found in this review.)

mediumLow.title: Baseline: PostgREST exposure is RLS-gated, not bare — 164/164 public tables have RLS enabled, all 5 views are security_invoker
mediumLow.evidence: get_advisors(security) returned 169 pg_graphql_anon_table_exposed + 169 pg_graphql_authenticated_table_exposed WARN lints. Catalog reconciliation: `select count(*) filter(where relrowsecurity) ... from pg_class where nspname='public' and relkind='r'` => {rls_enabled:164, rls_disabled:0, total:164}. The extra 5 objects are views; `pg_options_to_table(reloptions)` shows client_activity_summary, current_quarter_swots, user_kpi_dashboard, xero_bs_lines_wide_compat, xero_pl_lines_wide_compat ALL have security_invoker true/on and are owned by postgres => no owner-privilege RLS bypass. Conclusion: the 338 graphql exposure lints reflect anon/authenticated SELECT *grants*, but every row access is still adjudicated by RLS. Not a bare-exposure disaster; correctness of each policy is the residual risk (RLS-finder's dimension).
mediumLow.remediation: No action from the exposure lints alone. The linter cannot see RLS; treat these 338 WARNs as expected noise for a Supabase app that relies on RLS. Residual risk lives in per-policy correctness (handed to the RLS finder), not in the grants themselves.

mediumLow.title: Baseline + regression PASS: 48 SECURITY DEFINER functions in public, 40 grant anon / 42 grant authenticated; the five fixed today are confirmed revoked
mediumLow.evidence: `select count(*) from pg_proc where prosecdef and nspname='public'` => 48 total; 40 have has_function_privilege('anon','EXECUTE'), 42 have authenticated EXECUTE. Regression check on the five fixed 23-Aug: reset_user_password, create_app_user, create_client_account, complete_user_setup, create_test_user ALL return anon=false, auth=false => the revoke is LIVE in the catalog, no regression. get_advisors independently omits all five from its anon_security_definer_function_executable list (40 functions, none of them the fixed five). The 40 anon-executable definers (incl. auth_* RLS helpers, and write-capable save_assumptions_and_materialize / create_active_forecast_locked) require per-function guard adjudication — that is the definer-function finder's dimension, not this one.
mediumLow.remediation: None here — baseline handoff. Definer-function finder should adjudicate the 40 anon-executable + 42 authenticated-executable definers for internal auth guards and write primitives.

mediumLow.title: Advisor: 9 updated_at trigger functions have mutable search_path (but all are SECURITY INVOKER, so no privilege escalation)
mediumLow.evidence: get_advisors(security) flagged 9 function_search_path_mutable WARNs. Catalog check confirms all 9 have prosecdef=false (SECURITY INVOKER): update_report_templates_updated_at, update_xero_accounts_updated_at, update_cashflow_settings_updated_at, update_cashflow_account_profiles_updated_at, update_cashflow_statement_classification_updated_at, update_cfo_report_status_updated_at, update_consolidation_groups_updated_at, update_fx_rates_updated_at, update_xero_balance_sheet_lines_updated_at. Separately verified 0 of the 48 SECURITY DEFINER functions have a mutable search_path (the dangerous class is clean). Because these run as the invoking role, a search_path hijack cannot cross a privilege boundary — an attacker would only shadow objects within their own session.
mediumLow.remediation: Defense-in-depth: add `SET search_path = ''` (or `pg_catalog, public`) to each trigger function via ALTER FUNCTION. Low priority given they are invoker-context triggers, not definers.

mediumLow.title: Advisor: leaked-password protection (HaveIBeenPwned) disabled in Supabase Auth
mediumLow.evidence: get_advisors(security) returned auth_leaked_password_protection WARN: HIBP compromised-password checking is off. This is an account-hygiene config, not a reachable data-access path; it weakens resistance to credential-stuffing but does not itself expose client data.
mediumLow.remediation: Enable Leaked Password Protection in Auth > Policies (Matt to toggle in the WisdomBI Supabase dashboard). Consider a minimum password strength policy at the same time.

mediumLow.title: Advisor: 3 deprecated_*_backup tables have RLS enabled but no policy — fail-closed (safe), but they still hold retired client data
mediumLow.evidence: get_advisors(security) rls_enabled_no_policy INFO on the three tables. RLS-enabled + zero policies = default-deny for anon and authenticated (only service_role / postgres can read). So there is no anon/authenticated read path today. Flagged only because these are 'deprecated_*_backup' snapshots of real client assessment/KPI data sitting in the live prod DB.
mediumLow.remediation: Confirm these backups are still needed; if not, drop them to shrink the sensitive-data blast radius. If retained, leave RLS-with-no-policy (fail-closed) as-is — do NOT add a permissive policy.

mediumLow.title: Permissive USING(true) SELECT policies grant every authenticated user 3 reference/catalog tables (not tenant financial data)
mediumLow.evidence: `select ... from pg_policies where qual in ('true','(true)')` returns SELECT policies for role {authenticated}: kpi_definitions.kpi_definitions_select_consolidated, deprecated_kpi_benchmarks.kpi_benchmarks_select_consolidated, deprecated_swot_templates 'Authenticated users can view swot templates'. Also two INSERT-with_check=true policies (client_error_logs.insert_errors, forecast_audit_log.forecast_audit_log_insert) that let any authenticated user append log/audit rows. All are shared reference catalogs or append-only logs, not per-client financial rows, so USING(true) is intentional and not a cross-tenant leak. Handed to the RLS finder to confirm none of these tables carries tenant-scoped data.
mediumLow.remediation: No change if these remain pure shared-reference/append-log tables. RLS finder should confirm kpi_definitions/benchmarks contain no business_id-scoped rows; if they ever gain a tenant column, replace USING(true) with a tenant predicate. The forecast_audit_log INSERT(true) should ideally constrain with_check to rows the caller can access, to prevent forged audit entries.

mediumLow.title: Unauthenticated SECURITY DEFINER RPC poisons any business's account→category mappings
mediumLow.evidence: pg_get_functiondef: prosecdef=true, search_path='', body is a bare INSERT INTO public.account_category_patterns(business_id,...) VALUES(p_business_id,...) ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET category=p_category — no auth.uid()/ownership check. proacl grants anon. Definer write bypasses RLS. mediumLow.title: Unauthenticated SECURITY DEFINER RPC injects/manipulates Xero sync jobs for any business (sync DoS)

All low-impact (UI state / empty rows / a counter).

mediumLow.title: CONFIRMED: five account-management definers correctly revoked; RLS/role helpers safe-by-guard; all definers have search_path
mediumLow.evidence: All five today-fixed functions now show proacl 'postgres=X/postgres | service_role=X/postgres' only — no anon/authenticated — NO REGRESSION. The anon-granted RLS helpers (auth_can_access_business, auth_get_accessible_business_ids, auth_is_super_admin, auth_is_coach_of/owner_of, rls_user_owned/coached_businesses, can_access_process, is_coach, user_has_role, get_user_system_role) all gate on auth.uid() and return empty/false for anon — they MUST stay anon-callable because RLS policies invoke them during evaluation. get_all_users() is guarded by `IF NOT public.is_super_admin() THEN RAISE EXCEPTION`. mark_task_complete/mark_idea_status raise 42501 when auth.uid() IS NULL and re-check row visibility — properly guarded. Every one of the 47 SECURITY DEFINER functions has proconfig search_path set (public or ''), so there are NO search-path-hijack findings; the 9 function_search_path_mutable advisor warnings are all update_*_updated_at trigger fns that are SECURITY INVOKER, not definer.
mediumLow.remediation: No action on these. Use them as the template: the DEF-01..DEF-10 fixes should mirror the {postgres,service_role}-only ACL applied to the five account functions today.

mediumLow.title: Default privileges auto-grant EXECUTE-to-anon on every future public function and full DML-to-anon on every future postgres-owned table — the systemic root cause of the recurring 'definer function leaks to anon' incident class
mediumLow.object: pg_default_acl (schema public, objtypes f and r)
mediumLow.evidence: pg_default_acl for schema public: objtype 'f' owner postgres = '{postgres=X/postgres,anon=X/postgres,authenticated=X/postgres,service_role=X/postgres}' (and an identical row for owner supabase_admin), and objtype 'r' (tables) owner postgres = '{...anon=arwdDxtm/postgres,authenticated=arwdDxtm/postgres...}'. Consequence: every new function postgres creates in public is auto-granted EXECUTE to anon+authenticated (this is why a DROP+CREATE re-acquires the anon grant, exactly the mechanism CLAUDE.md's 're-issue revokes after every DROP+CREATE' fights), and every new postgres-owned table is auto-granted full DML (INSERT/SELECT/UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE/REFERENCES/TRIGGER) to anon — so a table where a dev forgets ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY is world-writable by anon. Currently no public table has RLS disabled (verified: only deprecated_*_backup are RLS-on/zero-policy = fail-closed), so no live table exposure — but security rests entirely on RLS discipline plus per-function manual revokes.
mediumLow.remediation: ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA public REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTIONS FROM anon, authenticated; (for both the postgres and supabase_admin default-ACL rows) so new definer functions default to closed and must be explicitly opened. Keep the CI check that fails any migration granting anon on a SECURITY DEFINER function. Consider a migration-lint gate asserting relrowsecurity on every new public table given the standing anon DML default.

mediumLow.title: extensions.pg_stat_statements is SELECT-granted to PUBLIC and anon holds USAGE on the extensions schema — query-text/parameter leak, but not PostgREST-exposed
mediumLow.evidence: information_schema.role_table_grants: extensions.pg_stat_statements and _info have grantee=PUBLIC, privs=SELECT. has_schema_privilege shows anon+authenticated have USAGE on schema 'extensions'. pg_stat_statements can expose normalized SQL text (and, in some captures, literals) across all tenants. However PostgREST exposes only public/graphql_public (+ storage's own API); 'extensions' is not in the exposed-schema set, and the anon/authenticated roles cannot open a raw SQL session, so there is no API path to SELECT it. Reachable only by a role with direct DB connection (service_role/postgres), not anon over HTTPS.
mediumLow.remediation: Defense-in-depth: REVOKE SELECT ON extensions.pg_stat_statements, extensions.pg_stat_statements_info FROM PUBLIC. No exposed path today, so low urgency.

mediumLow.title: All public views are security_invoker=on and all public tables have RLS enabled — no RLS-bypassing view or exposed table found (coverage/clean)
mediumLow.evidence: pg_class reloptions for the 5 public views: client_activity_summary, current_quarter_swots, user_kpi_dashboard all reloptions=['security_invoker=true']; xero_bs_lines_wide_compat, xero_pl_lines_wide_compat reloptions=['security_invoker=on']. All owned by postgres but security_invoker means SELECT runs with the caller's privileges, so underlying-table RLS still applies — no postgres-owned invoker-off view leaking client data. No materialized views in public. Separately, NOT c.relrowsecurity over public.relkind='r' returned zero rows (every public table has RLS enabled); the only RLS-on/zero-policy tables are deprecated_assessments_backup, deprecated_kpi_definitions_backup, deprecated_strategic_kpis_backup, which are fail-closed (deny-all) to anon/authenticated.
mediumLow.remediation: No action. Maintain the invariant: any new public view over client data must set security_invoker=on, and any new table must ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY (see GRANT-03).

mediumLow.title: No outbound/capability extension (http, pg_net, dblink, pg_cron) installed; supabase_vault schema is not anon/authenticated-usable
mediumLow.evidence: pg_extension: pg_graphql (graphql), pg_stat_statements (extensions), pgcrypto (extensions), plpgsql (pg_catalog), supabase_vault (vault), uuid-ossp (extensions). No http/pg_net/dblink/pg_cron present, so no anon-reachable SSRF/outbound or arbitrary-capability primitive. has_schema_privilege confirms anon=false, authenticated=false USAGE on schema 'vault' — decrypted secrets are not reachable by API roles. pgcrypto/uuid-ossp are benign compute functions.
mediumLow.remediation: No action. If pg_net or http is ever added, install it in a non-exposed schema and withhold EXECUTE from anon/authenticated.

mediumLow.title: Per-business data endpoints trust the coach role globally, not scoped to assigned_coach_id (latent cross-coach exposure)
mediumLow.object: src/app/api/kpis/route.ts, forecast/[id]/route.ts, annual-plan/route.ts, subscription-budgets/route.ts, goals/resolve-business/route.ts, monthly-report/*
mediumLow.evidence: Every per-business service-role route grants access when system_roles.role IN ('coach','super_admin') regardless of business assignment, e.g. kpis/route.ts:75 verifyBusinessAccess() -> verify-business-access.ts returns true for ANY super_admin (line ~67) and the inline variants (annual-plan/route.ts:55-58, subscription-budgets/route.ts:190-196 authoriseBusinessAccess, forecast/[id] resolver, resolve-business/route.ts:60-66) return true for role==='coach' with NO assigned_coach_id predicate. In contrast the CLIENT LISTING is assignment-scoped: coach/clients/route.ts:544 .eq('assigned_coach_id', user.id) and clients/send-invitation/route.ts:52. So a coach who is NOT assigned to a business can still read its financials by passing that business_id directly to a data endpoint. Catalog check: system_roles today = 21 client, 2 super_admin, 1 coach (all internal staff), so with a single coach there is no active client-vs-client leak; this becomes reachable the moment a 2nd independent coach account is created. Consolidation routes document this as intentional ('any coach/super_admin is trusted with any connection', consolidation/tenants/[connectionId]/route.ts:14-16).

If coaches should only see assigned clients, add an assigned_coach_id / business_users scope to the coach branch of verifyBusinessAccess and the inline authorise* helpers (super_admin may remain global). If coaches are intentionally global, document it and drop the assignment scoping from coach/clients GET for consistency. No change needed while exactly one coach exists, but add a regression test before onboarding a second coach.

mediumLow.title: Six service-role routes bypass the Phase-47 withSchema/withQuerySchema Zod wrappers
mediumLow.object: forecast/cashflow/settings GET, forecast/cashflow/profiles GET, Xero/sync GET, consolidation/fx-rates GET, forecasts/scenarios GET+DELETE
mediumLow.evidence: CLAUDE.md states 'All API routes use the Phase-47 withSchema/withQuerySchema Zod wrappers.' These export raw handlers instead: forecast/cashflow/settings/route.ts:65 `export async function GET`, forecast/cashflow/profiles/route.ts:39, Xero/sync/route.ts:205, consolidation/fx-rates/route.ts:117, forecasts/scenarios/route.ts:95 (GET) and :266 (DELETE). Not exploitable for cross-tenant access: each still performs its own auth gate (e.g. forecasts/scenarios/route.ts:80 .or owner/coach, Xero/sync verifyUserAccess at 222/247) and all query inputs feed parameterized PostgREST .eq() filters, so there is no injection or authz-bypass path — this is a convention/hardening deviation only.

mediumLow.title: PostgREST .or() filters built by template interpolation (injection-shaped, currently safe)
mediumLow.object: monthly-report/consolidated*, generate, forecasts/scenarios, forecasts/export, consolidation/businesses/[id], Xero/callback, Xero/complete-connection
mediumLow.evidence: Filter strings are assembled with template literals, e.g. monthly-report/consolidated/route.ts:126 .or(`owner_id.eq.${user.id},assigned_coach_id.eq.${user.id}`), forecasts/scenarios/route.ts:80, Xero/callback/route.ts:64 .or(`id.eq.${businessId},business_id.eq.${businessId}`), Xero/complete-connection/route.ts:149. mediumLow.evidence: getSupabaseSecretKey() (keys.ts) reads SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY / SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY / SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY — none NEXT_PUBLIC-prefixed. # WISDOMBI PRODUCTION DATABASE — FINAL SECURITY AUDIT (uudfstpvndurzwnapibf, 24 Aug 2026)

Access: read-only catalog + code reasoning. No function was executed against prod. All ACL/prosecdef/proconfig facts below re-confirmed live in one consolidated `pg_proc` query at audit close (oids cited).

## 1. EXECUTIVE VERDICT

**The read side is tight; the write side is not.** Tenant isolation for *reads* is soundly built and I found no cross-tenant read leak: 164/164 public tables have RLS enabled, all 5 public views are `security_invoker=on` (no owner-privilege view bypass), and — critically for this codebase — the dual-ID hazard is **neutralized at the RLS layer**, not exploitable: `auth_get_accessible_business_ids()` unions both `businesses.id` and `business_profiles.id` into one uuid[], so `business_id = ANY(...)` is correct regardless of which id-space a table's column uses (verified for `xero_connections`/businesses-space and `sync_jobs`/profiles-space). The five account-management definers fixed 23 Aug are **confirmed still revoked, no regression** (reset_user_password/create_app_user/create_client_account/complete_user_setup/create_test_user all now `{postgres, service_role}` only, anon_exec=false, auth_exec=false — oids 16519/16497/16499/16496/16501). [BASE-01, VIEW-05, RLS dim, DEF-00]

**The single worst thing:** a class of `SECURITY DEFINER` write RPCs in the PostgREST-exposed `public` schema that carry `EXECUTE` to `anon` (and several to `PUBLIC`) with **no internal authorization check**. Because a definer function runs as `postgres` and bypasses RLS, a direct `POST /rest/v1/rpc/<fn>` with the public anon key (which ships in the browser bundle) sidesteps every app-route ownership check. The two most dangerous are **`save_assumptions_and_materialize`** (oid 147803 — overwrites `financial_forecasts.assumptions` and, on `p_force_full_replace=true`, DELETEs non-manual `forecast_pl_lines` then rewrites caller-supplied P&L) and **`create_active_forecast_locked`** (oid 148881 — deactivates a business's live forecast and injects an attacker-shaped `is_active=true` row). Both confirmed anon_exec=true AND auth_exec=true, SECURITY DEFINER.

**Why HIGH, not CRITICAL (non-inflated):** the destructive write is gated on supplying a *valid existing id* the attacker does not have a reachable way to enumerate. `financial_forecasts` reads are RLS-scoped to `authenticated` only (no anon policy → anon SELECT default-denies), forecast_ids are 122-bit random UUIDs, and `financial_forecasts.business_id` FKs to `business_profiles(id)` so a guessed id fails the FK and the whole single-transaction body rolls back. So there is **no self-contained unauthenticated-to-specific-victim path** — it requires an out-of-band known id (or an authenticated tenant who already holds another tenant's business_profiles.id, which appears in app URLs/payloads). That is exactly the rubric's HIGH band ("definer write primitive with weak guard" AND "needs a known id"). **Caveat that would escalate to CRITICAL:** if *any* anon-readable view/function elsewhere leaks a forecast_id or business_profiles.id, the gate falls and these return to CRITICAL. None was found in this review, but the systemic default-privilege posture (GRANT-03) means new leaks can appear silently.

Bottom line: not a breach-in-progress, but a standing set of unauthenticated write/DoS/tamper primitives against client financial data that should be closed promptly. Confidence high on the catalog facts; the "not CRITICAL" rests on the absence of an id-leak, which is an ongoing invariant to protect, not a permanent guarantee.

## 2. RANKED REMEDIATION PLAN

### Group A — Quick-win REVOKEs (migration; safe, no legitimate caller relies on the anon/PUBLIC grant)
Every function below is called only from server routes that already run their own `getUser()` + business-access check via the RLS-respecting or service-role client; the anon/PUBLIC EXECUTE grant is superfluous attack surface. Pattern: `REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.<fn>(<sig>) FROM anon, authenticated, PUBLIC;` leaving `{postgres, service_role}` (mirror the 23-Aug account-function fix). **Re-issue the REVOKE after any DROP+CREATE** (DROP discards the ACL — CLAUDE.md invariant). Order by severity:

1. **`save_assumptions_and_materialize(uuid,jsonb,jsonb,boolean)`** — HIGH. [RLS-01, DEF-01, GRANT-02] oid 147803. Highest priority: it is the one with a destructive DELETE path.
2. **`create_active_forecast_locked(uuid,integer,text,jsonb)`** — HIGH. [RLS-02, DEF-02, GRANT-01] oid 148881. Match its sibling `activate_forecast_locked`, which already has anon_exec=false (oid 156095).

## 3. WHAT THIS AUDIT DID NOT COVER (honest coverage boundary)
- **Supabase Auth dashboard config** beyond the two lints surfaced (JWT/session settings, MFA enforcement, email/SMS provider config, redirect allow-lists, RLS on `auth.*`, SAML/SSO) — not inspectable from the SQL catalog.
- **Secrets management & rotation** — whether CRON_SECRET, the service-role/secret key, or Xero OAuth client secrets have leaked or need rotation; only that the secret key is confined to server-only code (AUTHZ-04) was verified.
- **Network / transport / platform** — Vercel edge config, CORS, rate-limiting/WAF, PostgREST server config (the actual `db-schemas`/`pgrst.*` GUCs were not readable from the DB; anon reachability of `public` RPCs is *inferred* from Supabase defaults + the fact the 5 prior account RPCs were anon-exploitable — treat as confirmed but not GUC-verified).
- **No live penetration testing / no exploit execution** — every finding is reasoned from catalog + code per the read-only mandate; no function was called to confirm, so exploitability is argued, not demonstrated.
- **`storage.*` and non-`public` exposed schemas** (`graphql_public`, `realtime`) policies — only `public` was audited in depth.
- **The 3 trigger-return definers** (`audit_employee_changes`, `log_forecast_change`, `notify_coach_forecast_complete`) — not usefully RPC-callable, judged low-risk, not deep-analyzed.
- **Xero OAuth connect-initiation route** (which HMAC-signs `state`) was not fully read; the callback trusts the signed business_id, so any missing check would live at the connect route — flagged as a residual, not cleared.
- **Data-content review** (PII minimization, retention, encryption-at-rest posture of the deprecated backup tables' contents) — out of scope.
